fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Closing a **bug** ticket sprays `Error: Ambiguous prefix '<4hex>' matches multiple tickets`
lines at the terminal and then leaves the CLI running for minutes after the close has already
committed durably. Reproduced twice (2026-08-08, 2026-08-10) with fragments `b2bb`, `28f9`,
`a9dd`, `dbb2`, `3e8b`, `03ef`, `94a3`, `c5b3`, `18ae`, `4527`; each time the operator had to
interrupt the process after confirming the status change had landed.

This ticket originally attributed the noise to the enrichment drain. That is **wrong**, and the
correction is recorded in a triage comment: the drain subtree
(`_store/event_append.py:606` -> `llm/enrich_drain.py:216` -> `drain` -> `llm/enrich.py`)
resolves only ticket ids that came from `os.listdir(tracker)`, i.e. already-canonical directory
names that short-circuit on the fast path at `_ids.py:239-241` and never reach the prefix
branch that prints. It has no prose scanner at all, and in async mode its stderr goes to
`.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log`.

## Approach

Both symptoms are ONE defect in `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, the optional `caused_by`
derivation invoked from `_commands/transition_close.py:246-248` **after** a bug close commits.
`_find_fixing_commit` walks the entire branch history and calls `_resolves_to` per commit;
`_resolves_to` re-resolves `bug_id` on **every** commit, and every candidate from
`verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (whose second source is the leading `<token>:` of the
commit subject) is resolved with no `quiet=`, no cache, and no shape filter. Any candidate that
is not a full/short/Jira id falls through to `_scan_alias`, which opens up to two JSON files
for each ticket directory.

Measured on this checkout: 3823 ticket directories, 2137 commits, 620 of them carrying a bare
`<4hex>:` subject (487 distinct), and ~0.26s per unresolvable candidate. The per-commit
`bug_id` re-resolution alone is ~2137 x 0.26s ~= 9 minutes of pure alias scanning. That is the
"hang": an unbounded O(commits x tickets) scan, not a deadlock.

Four changes, none of which alter WHICH id forms resolve:

1. Pass `quiet=True` at EVERY scanner call site in the module — `_resolves_to` (`blame.py:53`
   and `:55`), `_commit_ticket` (`:100`, the culprit commit's own subject), and the final
   self-comparison in `derive_caused_by` (`:135`) — using the seam `_ids.py:221-230` already
   documents for "scanners resolving candidates the user never supplied", the same treatment
   `_commands/close_precheck.py:119` already applies. Kills the terminal noise. All four are
   required: `_commit_ticket` is a SECOND scanner over commit-message candidates, so leaving it
   loud would keep a residual path that violates AC 1.
2. Hoist the `bug_id` resolution out of the per-commit loop (it is loop-invariant).
3. Memoize ref -> resolution for the duration of one derivation, as `close_precheck` does.
4. Short-circuit on a **necessary condition** before touching the store: a ref of hex-quad
   shape can only resolve to the target if the target's canonical id starts with it. This is
   provably semantics-preserving and is restricted to 1-, 2-, and 4-quad hex forms, which
   cannot collide with an alias (aliases are `adj-noun` or `adj-noun-noun` from the wordlist,
   or an 8-hex no-dash fallback) — 3-quad forms are deliberately excluded and still take the
   real resolver. Because that is a cross-module invariant owned by `_ids`/`_alias`, the guard
   carries a comment naming its source and a test asserts no generatable alias can take the
   hex-quad shape the short-circuit rejects, so the optimization cannot silently drift.

Separately, sweep the docs to stop advertising bare 4-digit (single-quad) references, per the
operator decision: name alias (preferred), 8-digit two-quad prefix, full canonical id, and
Jira/bridge ids as the reference forms. Compatibility resolution is unchanged and stays
documented as compatibility.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py` — the four changes above.
- `tests/unit/` — new regression tests.
- `src/rebar/_ids.py` — **module docstring only** (no code change): it is the one place that
  literally advertises "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as a supported form.
- `AGENTS.md` — the ticket-identifier authoring paragraph (:66-73). It does NOT advertise a
  bare 4-digit form today (it already discourages copying a short hex prefix and already frames
  short forms as compatibility), so this is an ADDITION: positively name the preferred forms,
  including the 8-digit two-quad prefix, which the file never mentions.

A repo-wide survey found the advertising surface is small: those two places. The ~420 bare
4-hex mentions elsewhere in `docs/` are incidental HISTORICAL citations of specific tickets
("epic 716f", "bug 84aa"), not guidance telling a reader to use that form, so they are out of
scope — rewriting them would be a large no-value diff. `docs/cli-reference.md:387`
(`rebar resolve <id_or_alias_or_prefix>`) is generated from `src/rebar/_cli/help/resolve.txt`
and says "prefix" generically, which correctly includes the PREFERRED 8-digit two-quad prefix,
so it is left alone.

Explicitly NOT changed: `_ids.py` resolution semantics, `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs`
(commit-subject candidates keep resolving exactly as today), the close gate, and the `Verified`
trailer check. No id form gains or loses the ability to resolve.

## Testing

- A commit message whose subject is a bare `<4hex>:` prefix that matches multiple tickets
  produces **no** `Ambiguous prefix` text on stderr during `derive_caused_by`.
- A bounded-work test: over a synthetic history of many commits carrying distinct 4-hex
  subjects, the number of underlying `resolve_ticket_id` calls stays small and constant rather
  than growing with the commit count (asserted by counting calls through a patched resolver).
- Behavior preservation: `derive_caused_by` still finds the fixing commit and the culprit
  ticket when the commit cites the bug by full canonical id, by 8-hex two-quad prefix, by
  alias, and by an unambiguous bare 4-hex prefix.
- A ref that is a hex-quad shape but NOT a prefix of the target still returns "no match", and a
  3-quad hex form still reaches the real resolver.
- A culprit commit whose OWN subject is an ambiguous bare 4-hex prefix also produces no
  `Ambiguous prefix` text (the `_commit_ticket` path).
- An alias-shape guard test: no alias generatable from the wordlist can take the 1-, 2-, or
  4-quad hex shape the short-circuit rejects.
- Docs: an assertion-style check that the swept files no longer present bare 4-digit ids as a
  recommended reference form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Closing a bug emits no `Ambiguous prefix` diagnostics for commit-subject candidates the
      user never supplied.
- [ ] `derive_caused_by` performs work bounded by the number of DISTINCT candidate refs rather
      than re-resolving per commit, proven by a call-count regression test.
- [ ] Every id form that resolves today still resolves: full canonical id, 8-hex two-quad
      prefix, alias, Jira key, and unambiguous bare 4-hex.
- [ ] The original post-close reproduction, replayed as a regression test over a synthetic
      multi-commit history, emits no `Ambiguous prefix` text and resolves each DISTINCT ref at
      most once (no per-commit re-resolution of the bug id).
- [ ] A regression test asserts that no alias generatable from the wordlist (`adj-noun`,
      `adj-noun-noun`, or the 8-hex no-dash fallback) can take the 1-, 2-, or 4-quad hex shape
      rejected by the short-circuit, so the optimization cannot silently drift.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_ids.py`'s module docstring no longer presents "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as
      a plain supported form, and `AGENTS.md`'s ticket-identifier paragraph positively names the
      preferred forms (alias / 8-digit two-quad prefix / full canonical id / Jira ids) while
      retaining its existing compatibility framing.
